featured_reviews.name: Kamlesh Gadilohar
featured_reviews.review_text:
1/5 – One of the Worst Mughlai Dining Experiences We've Had

We visited Delhi Darbar, Jogeshwari West for my brother's birthday celebration, expecting the quality and hospitality associated with the Delhi Darbar name. Unfortunately, it turned out to be one of the most disappointing dining experiences we've had.

We started with roasted and fried papad. The roasted papad had a small hair on it. I quietly removed it without informing my family to avoid spoiling the occasion, but such hygiene lapses should never happen.

For starters, we ordered the Shahi Kebab Platter, Mutton Kebab, and Finger Chips. The kebabs were the only items that tasted genuinely good, although the quantity was quite small. Even the Finger Chips portion was surprisingly small considering the pricing.

The rest of the food was disappointing:

Veg Crispy was overloaded with oil and had the smell of reused cooking oil. We hardly ate any of it and packed almost the entire dish. Nobody from the staff bothered to ask whether there was an issue.
Chicken Schezwan Tandoori seemed to be prepared using stale tandoori chicken.
Butter Chicken was very average and lacked the richness expected from a reputed Mughlai restaurant.
Mutton Masala was swimming in oil and had an ordinary taste.
Paneer Tikka Biryani contained hard paneer pieces, excessive oil, and very little flavor.
The Chicken Dum Biryani was the biggest disappointment. The rice quality was shockingly poor, consisting largely of broken "tukda" rice that we wouldn't even use for khichdi at home. It was excessively oily and filled with potato pieces. For a restaurant known for Mughlai cuisine, serving a biryani of this quality is simply unacceptable.

The service was equally disappointing. At one point, one of our family members had to get a plate himself because the attending manager was busy on a phone call. The manager came across as rude, inattentive, and unprofessional. Basic hospitality and customer service seemed completely missing.

What made the experience even more frustrating was that despite several dishes being left unfinished, no one from the staff showed any concern or made an effort to understand whether there was a problem with the food.

Our bill exceeded ₹5,000, yet the overall quality of food and service was nowhere near the level expected for that price. My family and I have dined at numerous Mughlai restaurants across Mumbai over the years, ranging from small establishments to premium dining venues, and this was honestly one of the worst experiences we've had.

A birthday celebration that should have been memorable for the right reasons ended up being memorable for all the wrong ones.

Poor food quality, excessive use of oil, questionable freshness, hygiene concerns, small portions, indifferent service, and premium pricing that simply doesn't match the experience. Based on this visit, I would not recommend Delhi Darbar, Jogeshwari West.

The Chicken Biryani and Cafe Safar Special Falooda were okay.

They don’t have many cold drink options, but besides their ice cream menu, they also have some extra ice creams stored in the fridge.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently ordered the Butter Chicken Meal Box from this restaurant, and it turned out to be an excellent experience—especially considering I received it on an offer for under ₹200. The packaging was neat and secure, reflecting good attention to detail.

The meal itself was perfect for one person and included butter chicken, two tandoori rotis, a portion of chicken kebab, two small gulab jamuns, a flavourful chutney, onion and lemon slices, and even a small soft drink bottle. Both the kebab and the butter chicken were exceptionally well-prepared—rich, tender, and truly satisfying.

For such a pocket-friendly price, this meal felt like remarkable value for money. I thoroughly enjoyed the food and would gladly order it again.

featured_reviews.name: Ands Fabrication
featured_reviews.review_text:
If disappointment had a taste, it would be exactly like the food at Al Ayamna.
We ordered the Barakas Thaal and Mutton Chaap Barra Tandoori, and honestly, I’m still wondering how this place is even in business. The mutton was so tough and rubbery, it felt like a jaw workout session rather than a meal. Freshness? Completely missing. Flavor? Nowhere to be found.
The so-called “special” thaal was a joke—bland, poorly cooked, and absolutely not worth even half the price. The rotis were dry and lifeless, like they were made in the afternoon and served at night without any shame.
And let’s talk about pricing—₹3600+ for this? For what exactly? Bad food and regret?
This place is all hype and zero quality. If you enjoy wasting money and testing your patience, go ahead. Otherwise, do yourself a favor and stay far away.
One visit was more than enough. Never again.

featured_reviews.name: Adil khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst. Avoid Al Ayamna at all costs.

We found a sharp metal wire-like object in the mutton pulao we ordered. This is not just bad service — it’s a serious health hazard that could have caused injury.

This clearly shows poor hygiene standards and complete negligence in food preparation. Such incidents are unacceptable and dangerous.

I strongly urge others to think twice before dining here. This place needs strict quality control and accountability.

featured_reviews.review_text:

We had an absolutely fantastic experience here! We ordered the Ertugul Thaal, and it was truly massive easily enough for 6–7 people. Every item in the thaal was packed with rich flavors and perfectly cooked. If you love mutton, this is something you definitely cannot miss! 🤩

We also tried the Special Fruit Champagne 🍹 and it was super refreshing and delicious a perfect drink to go along with such a heavy and flavorful meal.

The place has a really nice vibe and is perfect to enjoy with family and friends 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦✨.

There was a small confusion with our starters we had ordered veg but were served non-veg by mistake. But the owner was extremely polite and understanding and quickly got it replaced without any hesitation. Great hospitality! 👏

I’ve been ordering from Go Biryan for the past 5 years and I’m very familiar with how their dishes usually taste, which is why I was quite disappointed with my recent order.

I ordered the Mutton Bori Style Biryani, Dal Bukhara, and three varieties of tikka. While the tikkas were good and tasted as expected, the biryani was extremely disappointing. featured_reviews.review_text:
Go Biryan is a growing delivery chain that focuses on offering delicious meals which can suit all pockets. The brand currently operates with 4 outlets and certainly plans expand further. With a wide spread of Appetizer, Curries, Biryanis and much more to choose from, you can be surely assured of a delightful experience. The range of Biryanis start from Prince which is apt for 1 person and it goes upto Kingdom which can cater to a larger group of about 8-10 people. In my opinion the portion size of a Pince biryani too is apt for 2 people if it is tagged along with an appetizer.

1)Veg Galouti Kebab: Definately a must try.
2)Paneer Pahadi Tikka: Great qualitu of paneer and perfect balance of flavours.
3)Paneer Roast Masala Biryani: Loaded with abundance of flavours in every bite.
4) Veg Afghani Biryani: Quite different than the routine biryani, but definately worth trying.
5)Cheese stuffed mushroom tikka: Literally melts in the mouth.

featured_reviews.name: Shreya Shirley
featured_reviews.review_text:
Your Go to place for all Biryani needs. The packaging is spill free and neat.
What we ordered:
- Paneer Tikka & Veggies Biryani: Has gravy like paneer Tikka with big soft paneer pieces and vegetables.

-Paneer Makhani: The sabzi has many paneer pieces with a gravy which is oozing with flavour in every bite. It comes with Tandoori Roti.

-Veg Afghani Biryani: Really liked the taste of this. Must try.

-Paneer Makhani Roll - This is a big fat roll suffered with various sauces and Paneer Makhni pieces. It is good for evening snacks.

-Gulab Jamun: The Gulab Jamuns were really soft and cooked to perfection.

Along with the whole order they sent two chocolate sticks complimentary, that was a really nice and tasty gesture!

I really liked the taste of all the dishes, will definitely try more soon!

featured_reviews.review_text: Go Briyani is an affordable delivery place. I tried their Hara bhara kebab which was nice with their Paneer Tikka Briyani and Paneer Makhani Briyani. We ended the meal with Gulab Jamun which was nice, warm, soft and delicious.

featured_reviews.name: Jay Munwar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Go Biryan! This place is totally my favorite place to order delicious biryani and lipsmacking north indian food.

Ordered food from here for dinner. Delivery was quick and order came with proper packaging which was spill proof and tamper proof. Also the delivery is really recommendable by zomato valet which was super fast. Food delivered was piping hot and fresh.

We tried the Paneer Roast Masala Biryani, Lasooni Palak Paneer and Paneer Makhani Biryani Meal Box. Loved the packaging which was sealed with proper plastic wrapping ensuring tamper proof and spill proof. Food was superb in taste and quantities they serve is really recommendable!

I loved the lasooni palak paneer which was great in taste and was a perfect match for the dinner. Paneer Biryani comes with raita. Taste was superb and it was cooked well. It had an amazing aroma. Paneer Makhani Biryani Meal Box was a great pick which comes with galouti kebabs, gulab jamun and Biryani. The quantity for meal box was decent for 1 -2 person.  Paneer Makhani Biryani had all of the classic flavours and tasted just amazing.

Overall whole meal from Go! Biryan was superb and worth ordering! Their North Indian food was droolworthy and satisfying meal. Definately gonna check this place out again for ordering online.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We had dinner at this outlet in Ramadhan.
If you're around Andheri, Persian Darbar is honestly a must-visit. The decor is beautiful has that royal, slightly old-school charm that makes the whole experience feel special.
The food was the real highlight though. Every dish felt like it was trying to outdo the other in flavour, and somehow nothing disappointed. What I really liked is that the staff actually guides you based on your mood and preferences instead of just pushing popular items. We went with their suggestions and it totally paid off. Portions are quite generous, so ordering smart helps. Their Mughlai dishes and kebabs especially stand out, and the richness is balanced well without feeling too heavy.
Service was smooth and attentive without being intrusive, which added to the overall relaxed vibe. It does get pretty busy, especially on weekends, so reserving a table in advance is a good idea.
Overall, great food, great vibe, and a place you’d want to come back to.
Enjoy your meal

featured_reviews.review_text:
Even at 3am on a weekend, this place proved why it’s a crowd favorite. We walked into an empty restaurant, and within 30 minutes it was buzzing with diners. The mutton seekh kebabs were freshly barbecued and absolutely delicious. The butter chicken struck the perfect balance—not overly sweet—and paired beautifully with hot, fluffy rotis. While the chicken biryani was unavailable, the mutton biryani made up for it, though slightly heavy on the garam masala.

On the server’s recommendation, we ended with freshly made kunafa at 4am, and it was truly out of this world. Huge kudos to the staff for serving such heartfelt food while most of Mumbai was fast asleep. ₹3,500 for five people felt well worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Nilesh Netke
featured_reviews.review_text:
Serious Food Safety Issue & Request for Accountability

We visited Persian Darbar expecting a good dining experience; however, it resulted in a serious health issue.

We ordered a combination of vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes. From the vegetarian items, Paneer Tikka Masala was partially left, packed, and taken home. The next day, all five of us who consumed the food suffered from loose motion, fever, and vomiting. Subsequently, our parents also consumed the same packed food and experienced identical symptoms.

This strongly points toward poor food quality or lack of freshness. Due to this incident:
•	Multiple family members required medical attention
•	We incurred doctor consultation and medication expenses
•	I missed work, and my parents also lost working days
•	We faced significant physical discomfort and mental stress

Dining at a reputed restaurant should create good memories—not lead to health trauma and medical emergencies.

Given the seriousness of this incident, we believe the management should take responsibility and compensate us for the medical expenses, lost workdays, and the distress caused. At the very least, we expect acknowledgment of the issue and assurance of corrective measures to prevent this from happening to other customers.

This review is shared in the interest of consumer awareness and accountability.

featured_reviews.name: Rishabh Vashist
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very rarely will you come across a place that nails all three - food, service and atmosphere. This is one of them.

Open till 4AM, Persian Darbar offers delicious (vegetarian here) options - the special persian biryani is to kill for and the classic cream kunafa is to die for.

In all my years, I have not tasted anything closer to perfection - the sweetness, texture, cream, everything goes so well together.

The aesthetics and the vibes are an added bonus. The kindness of the staff goes a long way as well.

I recommend add tejpatta and pls add Kevra water. Without these two essential ingredients you aren't cooking that yummy biryani we all wish we had ordered from some Khaansama.

The starters were a definite highlight—they were delicious and set a high bar for the rest of the meal. Similarly, the soup was excellent.

The true star of the evening, however, was the tawa item selection. These dishes were absolutely fantastic and brought a lot of flavor to the table. I highly recommend trying them out!

Overall, it was a great meal and a fun experience. I would certainly go back, especially for the starters and the tawa specialties!

At Biryani By Kilo, our Handi biryani is slow Dum-cooked using the choicest of ingredients, made fresh only on order. We deliver/serve Biryani in the same Handi in which it is Dum cooked on order to lock the delicious flavors, aromas & taste. BBK Kebabs, curries, breads & other Indian classical dishes are top notch too.
In today’s fast-paced world, we need to slow down and enjoy life’s precious moments, especially food. We believe that food must be relished with fursat, in every bite. So when you dig in to our food, it’s “Fursat Wala Yum, Dum Dumma Dum Dum”.'
We have 100+ outlets in 45+ cities and can be ordered through website, App, Call Centre (1800-212-2-212).

featured_reviews.name: Miura
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had previously tasted Veg Hyderabadi Biryani at a friend’s place, and it was absolutely delicious. Based on that experience, I decided to order Chicken Hyderabadi Dum Biryani on New Year at home.
The packaging was impressive and thoughtfully done. The biryani was delivered in a clay pot, along with raita, onions, and lemon, all neatly packed. Presentation-wise, it definitely stood out.
However, the taste was average. The biryani felt quite dry and lacked the rich flavors I was expecting. While the quality of ingredients was good, the quantity was on the lesser side and may not be sufficient for two people. Perhaps the taste variation was due to the heavy New Year rush. it is a budget-friendly option with good quality

I actually like the Biryani which Biryani Bu Kilo makes, their Salan and Raita really compliments any Biryani you order.
The staff at this store is very sweet, especially the manager, not only do the listen to feedback but also work on correcting it.
We ordered the Paneer Dum Biryani and with the Salan, Raita and Salad it was a treat to have.
Thank you team Biryani by Kilo
